central_claim: The FET-fusion -> impaired-ATM -> compensatory-ATR-dependency hypothesis, measured on other FET fusions in other diseases, is structurally eligible in EMC's commonest fusion types but the in-silico transfer support (tumour transcriptome, CRISPR dependency, drug-response) is weak-to-null, so this document reports no EMC-specific ATR vulnerability finding, only an assessment of whether the class hypothesis is internally consistent and transfers.

p1s.summary: The §3.4 table cell '27,196 (58.2%, was 662/1.0%)' for GSE4303/GPL3290 juxtaposes a PROBE count (27,196) with an ACCESSION-level resolution rate (58.2%), which are different denominators (41,614 probes-with-an-accession vs 65,180 distinct accessions) and are not related by simple division (27,196/41,614 = 65.4%, not 58.2%).
p1s.evidence: Source `emc-atr-vulnerability.json` -> part_b per-platform block for GSE4303-GPL3290: `n_probes_with_an_accession: 41614`, `n_distinct_accessions: 65180`, `accession_resolution_rate: 0.582` (=37911/65180), `n_mapped: 27196` (probes). Both numbers are individually correct against their own artifact fields (27196 matches n_mapped exactly; 58.2% matches accession_resolution_rate rounded), and the surrounding prose in §3.2a/§3.4 does separate 'accession resolution' from 'usable probes' as two distinct quantities before the table compresses them into one cell. So this is not a wrong number, but the compressed table-cell notation invites a reader to treat 58.2% as the fraction of 27,196-over-41,614, which it is not.
p1s.fix: Split the table cell into two clearly labelled figures, e.g. '27,196 probes mapped (accession resolution 58.2%; was 662 probes / 1.0% accession resolution)', or add a footnote clarifying the two different denominators, matching the disambiguation already present in the running prose.
